Но в ряде морфологических форм оно фиксировано на закрытом слоге: зу́нтту 'гора', хъу́нтIа, 'яма', буру́ккин 'забота', и словообразовательных суффиксах: къалайчи́ 'лудильщик', чича́ву 'писание', гъанма́ 'тот, который близок'.» ... Borise (carrying Murkelinskij 1971): "Stress facts are notoriously unclear in Lak. Stress in Lak interacts with vowel length, but because vowel length facts are not well-established and vary across Lak dialects (Khajdakov 1966: 118), stress patterns are also poorly understood. At the same time, there are clear QS tendencies: Lak stress is mobile and tends to target closed syllables and syllables containing long vowels or diphthongs, or geminated consonants; if there is more than one such syllable in a word, the rightmost one is stressed: dúk…

audit.action: cite a better source for the same coding
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: both deciding quotations are verbatim in held files — Murkelinskij 1967:490 §4 on the 300-dpi page image (page number visible) and Borise lines 294-302 of the held extracted text. (2) The classification 'weight-hedged' (weak, non-fixed, tied to vowel length/closed syllables; rightmost heavy, else final; suffixal exceptions) rests on a 1967 encyclopedic sketch at page grade plus the 1971 reference grammar carried through a 2018/2021 handbook survey. Every independent statement I could open today agrees: ILing RAS minlang page («слабое, непостоянное; связано с долготой гласного»), Shakhemirova 2010:206-207 («непостоянное... зависящее, в основном, от закрытости слогов и долготы гласного»), Kakvaeva 2020:7 (no clear dynamic stress). Nothing found suggests fixed stress; the only alternative in the literature is the Kibrik & Kodzasov 'phrasal prominence only' view, already carried
